name: CyberLogitec
tagline: Enterprise software for container shipping lines, port terminals and freight forwarders.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: This is not an app, it is a stack of enterprise systems that run ocean carriers, container terminals and forwarders: liner booking and documentation, terminal operations, yard and crane planning, EDI with customs and partners. The buyers are shipping lines and port operators, the contracts are multi-year implementations with consultants, and the price is whatever the sales engineer says it is. Nothing about it is a personal-use product, so there is nothing to one-shot a replacement for. An agent can build you a shipment tracker or a container ledger in an afternoon, and that is a different thing entirely. If you genuinely need a terminal operating system you are not shopping on a directory like this one.
coreLoopDIY: A local shipment and container ledger that tracks bookings, containers, milestones and documents, with CSV import and a simple timeline view.
requirements: Optional carrier tracking API keys if you want live milestones, otherwise manual entry
whatYouLose: EDI and EDIFACT messaging with carriers, customs authorities and port community systems
Terminal operations: yard planning, crane and vessel stowage, gate automation, equipment control
Regulatory and customs filing support across dozens of jurisdictions
Twenty-four seven support contracts and the implementation team that makes any of this work in a live port
Integration with the carrier and terminal systems your counterparties already run
moatNotes: The real product is the EDI plumbing and the fact that every counterparty in the lane already speaks to it.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because a terminal operating system is not software you evaluate, it is infrastructure you install. When cargo stops moving because your yard planner crashed, somebody has to answer the phone, and that somebody is contractually obligated. Customs filings, port community system handshakes and carrier EDI formats change constantly, and keeping up with them is a full-time department. Nobody is replacing that with a personal build, including the people who could technically write it.
notes: A shipment ledger is a one-sitting build; a terminal operating system is not. The moat is the EDI and customs plumbing plus the fact that every carrier, port and broker in the chain is already wired into it.
prompt:
Build a local-first shipment and container ledger. This is a personal consolation tool, not a terminal operating system.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Node 20, TypeScript, Fastify for the API
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/shipments.db
- React with Vite for the UI, plain CSS, no component library
- Single repo, npm run dev starts API on 3001 and UI on 5173

Data model:
- shipment: id, reference, mode (ocean | air | truck), origin, destination, carrier, etd, eta, status, notes
- container: id, shipment_id, container_number, type (20GP | 40GP | 40HC | reefer), seal_number, weight_kg
- milestone: id, shipment_id, code, label, actual_at, source (manual | import)
- document: id, shipment_id, filename, kind (bill_of_lading | packing_list | invoice | other), stored_path

Features that are in scope:
- CRUD for shipments and containers
- Add milestones manually, show a vertical timeline per shipment
- CSV import for shipments and containers, with a dry-run preview that lists rows it would reject and why
- Dashboard: shipments grouped by status, flag anything past ETA with no arrival milestone
- Document upload to ./data/docs, metadata in SQLite, no cloud storage
- Full text search across reference, container number and carrier
- Export everything to a single JSON file and reimport it

Explicitly out of scope, do not build these:
- No EDI, EDIFACT, ANSI X12 or customs filing
- No accounts, no login, no multi-tenant, no telemetry
- No live carrier API calls in v1, leave a clearly marked stub module at src/providers/tracking.ts with keys read from .env
- No yard, stowage, crane or gate logic

Ship a .env.example, a seed script with ten fake shipments, and a README that states in the first paragraph that this tracks shipments and does not move cargo.
